problem:
Consider the following data sets:

$$
x={6,\,4,\,8,\,6},\,y={4,\,7,\,11,\,14}
$$

You're given that $\overset{―}{x}=6$ and $\overset{―}{y}=9.$ Calculate $\text{Cov}(x,y).$

feedback.problem:
| **Year of Experience, in years ($x$)** | $1$ | $2$ | $2$ | $7$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Number of Strikes ($y$)** | $2$ | $1$ | $3$ | $6$ |

Four friends went bowling. The table above shows their years of bowling experience and the number of strikes they got in the game.
Compute the covariance of the data sets given that the means are $\overset{―}{x}=3$ and $\overset{―}{y}=3.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The (population) covariance of the data sets $x={{x}_{1},{x}_{2},…,{x}_{n}}$ and $y={{y}_{1},{y}_{2},…,{y}_{n}}$ is given by 

$$
\text{Cov}(x,y)=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}),
$$

where $\overset{―}{x}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{x}_{i}$ and $\overset{―}{y}=\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}{y}_{i}$ are the means of the data sets.

Therefore, the covariance of our data sets is

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}(x,y) & =\frac{1}{n}{\sum }_{i=1}^{n}({x}_{i}-\overset{―}{x})({y}_{i}-\overset{―}{y}) \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(1-3)(2-3)+(2-3)(1-3)+(2-3)(3-3)+(7-3)(6-3)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[(-2)(-1)+(-1)(-2)+(-1)(0)+(4)(3)] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}[2+2+0+12] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot 16 \\  & =4.\end{aligned}
$$
